A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDC-Agent work, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither contains appendix pages. V2 repeatedly refers to an absent appendix for prompts, pseudocode, generation analyses and overhead details, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: V1 reports original VDC benchmark results, component and training ablations, principle and iteration sensitivity experiments, and a qualitative comparison.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds DREAM-1K results, additional backbones, human preference evaluation and further controlled comparisons.

M1.justification: The generation, scoring, reflection, preference construction and curriculum DPO pipeline is retained. Equation (3) newly includes video x in both refinement calls, but the PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or clarifies previously implicit inputs. The referenced pseudocode is absent.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from VDC alone to include DREAM-1K, comprising 1,000 annotated clips with diverse complexities. This adds substantial independent video coverage. Cockatiel-4K training videos, the five caption dimensions and VDC-Agent-19K remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3-VL-8B and InternVL2.5-8B comparisons. DREAM-1K additionally includes Tarsier-7B and LLaVA-Video-7B. New controls include Best-of-N and anti-curriculum DPO. LLaVA-OneVision's existing VDC baseline is relocated, while vanilla DPO is renamed Random DPO.

E3.justification: V2 adds DREAM-1K event-level precision, recall and F1 evaluation; applies the framework to two additional backbones; and evaluates 500 randomly sampled preference pairs using three blind human raters and GPT-5.1 in both input orders. It also introduces inference-budget comparisons. Dataset-construction totals now refer to eight A800 GPUs rather than one.

E4.justification: New analyses examine preference validity, caption-length bias, evaluator position bias, reversed curriculum ordering and reflection versus Best-of-N under comparable time budgets. Principle robustness adds Shutterstock-derived P4, and principle/iteration studies extend to DREAM-1K. The original greenhouse qualitative example is retained, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. V2's separate human judgments and averaging across GPT input orders describe its evaluation protocol, without introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results, including 37.4 F1 on DREAM-1K and human preference rates of 67.6–75.8%, while retaining Qwen's VDC 49.08/2.50. Existing values also change: OwlCap's camera result becomes 46.90/2.50 from 41.30/2.20; Baseline+P2 becomes 45.43/2.30 from 45.83/2.32, and Baseline+P2+R becomes 46.15/2.34 from 46.55/2.36.

T1.justification: Equation (3) adds video x to the refinement/reflection arguments, but it is unclear whether this revises the mathematical definition or makes implicit conditioning explicit. The remaining definitions, DPO loss and curriculum objective are substantively unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: V2 broadens the abstract and introduction from state-of-the-art performance on VDC with one backbone to two benchmarks, cross-backbone generalization and human-validated preference quality. It also foregrounds faithfulness beyond caption length. Autonomous data generation, curriculum DPO and efficient internalization were already core contributions in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning scorer validity, length and position bias, grounding beyond VDCscore, premature exposure to difficult pairs, and directed reflection versus extra sampling. Some conclusions exceed the evidence: position-bias robustness is asserted despite GPT preference rates changing from 84.4% to 95.2% across input orders.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 32 sampled frames, 128 tokens per frame, beam size 1, temperature 0.1 and maximum caption length 1024, and supplies a project-page pointer. These are disclosures, not established changes to existing experiments. Most training settings remain unchanged; promised appendix prompts and pseudocode are unavailable.

R1.justification: The cited literature expands substantially, including Constitutional AI, Self-Refine, PromptAgent, self-rewarding models, curriculum learning and new benchmark/model references. Several earlier captioning citations disappear. Sections 2–3 gain broader connections to self-feedback and adaptation research, while retaining the central positioning against dependence on external teachers.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages and results narrative are rewritten; the agent-related-work discussion, qualitative discussion and conclusion are condensed. Author and affiliation information changes, and acknowledgements are added. These are extensive prose revisions despite retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Figure 1 is rearranged, Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, and a caption-length histogram is added. Tables gain backbone blocks, controls and DREAM-1K columns, alongside new comparison tables. The qualitative figure is relocated and reduced; several dense displays become noticeably smaller.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited validation: another benchmark and two additional backbones test generalization, human judgments assess the self-generated preferences, and new controls probe curriculum ordering and extra-compute explanations. These address important evidential gaps. Missing appendix details, smaller displays and overstrong bias conclusions remain weaknesses, but the broader and more targeted validation provides a substantial net quality improvement.
